doc: A site states its title, address, languages, routes and budget in its oweb.config.ts; every operation reads it and a request's options stand over it. Build a directory of pages into a site whose every route is its semantic tree written as HTML and as Markdown. Ask a site what it is, list its routes, read one page as an agent that only fetches would, and search every page's sections — of its source, without building it, or of the site as built: the directory a build wrote, read as it was published.

tools.name: site.build
tools.description: Build the site: each page of pages/ a route with its index.html (the tree as HTML: readable with no script) and index.md (the tree as Markdown), the routes table, llms.txt, the search index, 404.html for a lost address, given the site's address sitemap.xml, and the delivery manifest — every file as stored and as a static host sends it, each route's bytes before it reads held to a budget (over it: written, and failed with where). A link inside the site that leads nowhere fails the build with each one said, and nothing is written

site.description: a file or directory path: the site's directory (it holds pages/)

config.description: a file or directory path: the site's configuration, where it is not the oweb.config.ts in its directory: the same pages as another site — what it states beside the pages (an engine, a route's built page, a catalog) is from its own directory

out.description: a file or directory path: the directory written

title.description: the site's title (default: its first page's)

languages.description: its languages, the default first: en,zh — a first directory of that name is that language's pages

url.description: where it is served (https://example.org/docs/): the sitemap's addresses

readable.description: the most bytes a route sends before it reads, its index.html as gzip (default 100000; 0 holds none)

engine.description: a file or directory path: the program its pages load in a browser: a world's directory (omui build --web of oweb.reader) — served once from engine/, each page still its document until it takes the program

load.description: when a page takes the program where its route does not say: eager (default), idle, interaction

tools.name: site.describe
tools.description: What a site is, as it says it at each of its doors: its title, address and languages, each route with its title and its Markdown's address, the requests to go on with — and the text a build writes as llms.txt, the same words an agent that only fetches is given

url.description: where a source is served, where its configuration does not say: the addresses its description gives (a built site states its own)
